paragraphs: Here's what I love about this psalm, friend. David is a king with an army, and he still opens by praising the LORD as "my Rock," the One who trains his hands (Psalm 144:1). He doesn't say he's strong. He says the LORD is his fortress, his stronghold, his deliverer and his shield, the One he takes refuge in (Psalm 144:2). Everything David has, he pictures as coming from the LORD.

Then David gets honest about how small people are. "Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow" (Psalm 144:4). And right after that, he prays for rescue with his whole chest, because he knows who to run to. Even in the middle of that prayer, he says he will sing the LORD "a new song" (Psalm 144:9). I think that's the move for us, baker. Ask for help AND sing, in the same breath, before the answer shows up.

And look where David's picture ends: full storehouses, safe walls, and no cry of lament in the streets (Psalm 144:13-14). He calls the people of whom this is so blessed, and then he adds, "blessed are the people whose God is the LORD" (Psalm 144:15). So the big idea is this: a small, breath-sized life is held by a big Rock, and that is the heart of the blessing. Whatever you're facing today, you can take refuge in Him and start singing.
